maria chen: Hi folks — quick calendar mess up question. My calendar shows the orientation as 9:00 AM PST but the invite says 17:00 UTC. Which one is correct? I don’t want to miss the live Q&A.
jamal: Hey Maria — orientation is 9:00 AM Pacific / 17:00 UTC is the same, but sometimes Outlook on Windows shows the event in local time incorrectly if your machine timezone is set to something funky. What are you seeing?
eli: if you open the Google invite it should show both times under "More actions" -> "Copy to my calendar"; if you imported the .ics into Outlook it might've changed the timezone tag.
maria chen: I didn't import an ics — I accepted in Google Calendar from the company invite but my work Outlook calendar (sync) is showing 12:00 PM. Kinda panicked.
onboarding-bot: Reminder: Orientation recording will be posted to the #new-hires-docs drive within 2 hours after session ends. Retention 90 days. (See <https://redwood.company/onboarding/recordings>)
jamal: @maria chen — can you DM me a screenshot of both calendars? Also check Preferences -> Time zone in Outlook. I've seen VPNs force a different timezone.
maria chen: screenshot sent. Outlook is set to my local (CET) but Google is showing Pacific because company calendar uses the event with zone fixed. Looks like double conversion.
kayla (hr): We try to schedule live sessions at 9am PST to be somewhat friendly to EMEA, but if the calendar client reinterprets the timestamp you can get odd offsets. If you can't make the live Q&A we'll post questions in the form and the hiring manager will reply.
eli: Quick workaround: open the event in Google Calendar, click the three dots -> "Publish event" -> copy link. That link reliably shows correct start time in any browser.
jamal: Also note — the Zoom join URL in the invite should be canonical. If the time looks weird, join the Zoom link at the published start time (9:00am PST). If you try to join at the converted time your client may attempt to join earlier/later.
maria chen: thanks — one last thing: who can access the recording? I had an old company where recordings were restricted to presenter + admins.
onboarding-bot: Recording access policy: recordings are posted to the secure onboarding drive. Access = new-hires group + HR + hiring manager. External links are not public.
kayla (hr): If you need a manager/mentor to have a copy longer than 90 days, ping me and we can extend retention for that file.
maria chen: perfect, thanks. Also the recording link in the calendar sometimes has a passcode embedded in the URL — is that safe to share with managers?
devex: The embedded passcode in Zoom links is fine inside Redwood domains. If you need to share externally ask HR for a sanitized link.
jamal: For future-proofing — if you want the canonical schedule file do this: in Calendar, click "Download .ics" -> open in a text editor -> verify the "TZID:" lines. If TZID looks like "Europe/Paris" vs a fixed offset the import will be correct.
maria chen: noted. Appreciate the quick responses. I'll join 9:00am PST and watch the recording if timezone gremlins persist. :thumbsup:
eli: welcome aboard, Maria! See you in the session.
kayla (hr): Welcome! If anything else pops up, DM HR channel or me directly.
jamal: ping me if the calendar still acts up after the session, we can update the invite metadata.
